summary_en: Harry reached a junction where an older Slytherin boy waited in green-fringed black robes.
Harry recognized the Slytherin boy's face while wearing his Cloak of Invisibility.
Harry realized who had been waiting for him.
Harry told the boy he had been waiting for him.
The Slytherin boy jerked back and dropped his textbook.
The boy started to speak, saying "You're-".
Harry told him to say what he meant.
Lesath Lestrange asked if he had done the right thing by not stepping forward.
Harry reflected on how many ways he could kill his best friend by being stupid.
Lesath asked if he had been wrong.
Harry said Lesath had acted correctly and that he himself was the fool.
Lesath apologized to his lord.
Harry asked whether Lesath could have killed the troll.
Lesath asked whether he should study the Killing Curse.
Harry insisted he was not Lesath's lord.
Lesath replied yes, my lord.
Harry suggested Lesath learn to defend himself with the Defense Professor's help.
Lesath bowed and said he would follow Harry's orders.
Harry would have complained about being misunderstood, if he hadn't been understood perfectly.
Lesath left.
Harry stared at the wall.
Harry thought he had already figured out all the ways he had been stupid.
This had just been more overconfidence.
Harry's Slytherin side asked coldly if they understood what they did wrong.
Harry answered yes.
Slytherin said Harry's qualms made no sense and asked why he forgot Lesath.
Hufflepuff said having Lesath as a minion seemed Dark-Lordish.
Slytherin radiated contempt and showed an image of Hermione's corpse.
Harry screamed internally to stop it.
Slytherin suggested focusing on efficiency rather than seeming Dark-Lordish.
Harry conceded the point.
Slytherin said Harry would only listen after his next friend dies.
Harry worried he was going insane from the voices in his head.
The Boy-Who-Lived.
Pain.
Harry Verres trudged on alone.
Hurts.
Harry walked on through the silent corridors.
Professor Quirrell demanded to know how Mr. Potter was doing.
McGonagall said Potter had stopped guarding Granger's body and gone to dinner.
Quirrell demanded to know the boy's state, not physical.
McGonagall said she was about to order Quirrell out of her office.
Quirrell paced and argued that only Lupin might reach Potter now.
McGonagall said Lupin had restrained James Potter in Hogwarts days.
Quirrell said the disaster path must be averted at every point.
McGonagall told Quirrell she had reached her limits and he should go.
Quirrell said she would be the first he thought of after Granger.
McGonagall told Quirrell to leave if he had nothing more to say.
Quirrell asked if her confederacy had deduced who he really was.
McGonagall said yes, in fact.
Pure magic and power crashed into the room.
Hermione Granger's death certificates drifted to the floor.
David Monroe warned McGonagall that Potter could become dangerous.
McGonagall snapped that he would exercise courtesy in her office.
Quirrell said fear moved him and Potter could join rituals inscribed on tombstones.
McGonagall said the idea was ridiculous.
A wordless image of a patch of glass on a steel ball crossed her mind.
McGonagall said Potter would not do such a thing.
Quirrell said Potter may be reckless once resolved on a goal.
McGonagall asked if Quirrell had spoken to the Headmaster.
Quirrell said Dumbledore could not reach Potter and he would consult Snape.
